predecessors.name: Taifa of Murcia
predecessors.text: the Taifa of Albarracín, ceded by Muhammad ibn Mardanis, the 'Wolf King', to Pedro Ruiz de Azagra

successors.name: Crown of Aragon
successors.text: Albarracín and its lands, conquered by Peter III of Aragon in 1284 and 'officially incorporated into the Kingdom of Aragon' in 1300

ledger.x: 1167: Pedro Ruiz de Azagra receives Albarracín.
1167: Azagra holds Albarracín as a vassal of Sancho VI of Navarre; the page does not say the lordship paid tribute, so this reads the lord's vassalage as the lordship's.
September 1284: the siege ends in conquest; the House of Azagra's line is deposed.

September 1284: 'the Sinyoría d'Albarrazín was conquered by the Kingdom of Aragon' (Peter III); he gave the city to his illegitimate son Ferdinand, while Juan Núñez II de Lara kept up a claim until 1300.

wars.name: Siege of Albarracín (c. 1220)
wars.outcome: James I of Aragon besieged Albarracín during the First Noble Revolt and lifted the siege for want of noble support; no change.

wars.name: Aragonese conquest of Albarracín
wars.outcome: Peter III of Aragon conquered the lordship after a siege from April to September 1284, helped by the 1281 Treaty of Ágreda with Castile; Juan Núñez I de Lara's attempts to recover it, with French help, failed.

certainty.note: The pages name Albarracín and no frontier; the extent is a radius around the city.
